output.summary: A perennial flowering herb native to Europe, common comfrey grows in damp grassland and beside rivers and ditches. Its stems are bristly, while its tubular flowers are usually cream-yellow or pink-purple. Despite mild toxicity and potential liver harm, its leaves and shoots have been considered edible, even raw; stalks are said to be best gathered before flowering and blanched before steaming.
